findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

The antenna cable for the boom-box radio in the kitchen is observed looping over cleaned/sanitized spatulas on the magnetic rack next to the dish room doorway. This is not a regularly sanitized surface and should not be in contact with food or non-food (magnetic rack) contact surfaces. The cord was removed from the location and the items re-sanitized to correct.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

On arrival, no CFPM is available in the kitchen. No CFPM arrived during the inspection to correct. Manager at this time is new to the position and in the process of taking the course. Follow up on the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 (C) (P) (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HAND WASHING SINK.
An employee was observed turning of the faucet without a clean barrier after washing their hands. Another was observed using a paper towel to urn off the faucet then use that same towel to dry off their hands. Hand washing procedures were discussed with the PIC and they were instructed to ensure education of the staff.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 (A) (Pf) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded at a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.
Cottage cheese was observed open and with a date mark of 4/29. Today is day 8 of the 7 days. Date marking rules were discussed and the container was discarded during the inspection.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

Observed the ice machine deflection plate to be beginning to accumulate slime. Discussed with the person in charge and instructed to maintain clean.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed the walk-in cooler temperature to be at 58F. PHFs within the cooler were probed between 50-54F. A rising trend was noted on the temperature logs since 05/08/2017. Maintenance stated the alarm failed to send the required email, but did not alarm until approximately 20 minutes prior to arriving (around 1:10 PM). Order of Destruction was initiated on all PHFs within the cooler. Maintenance stated the cooler condensor fan had failed and would be able to be fixed within the day.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750-140b Observed date markings on some 6-door cooler items to be beyond the seven days allowed for potentially hazardous and ready-to-eat foods. The foods were recently pulled from the freezer and did not have 'pulled/thawed' dates in place. Red meat sauce was dated 1/10, ham slices dates 1/12 and turkey is observed dated 1/13. Items were properly dated or put into use during the inspection.  Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed a crack in the wall above the dish machine.  Seal the crack. 
2) Observed an absence of caulk at the dish machine (right side). Re-caulk the dish machine.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed baked beans on the steam table at 111 F.  Beans were heated in the oven and had been on steam table line for ten minutes.  Beans were immediately put back into the oven and the steam table was turned up. The temperature rose above 135 F during the inspection.
750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.)

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed single service items intermixed.  Items must be stored in a manner to protect them from cross contamination.  Items were stored with the handle extended out.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
Observed a large container of veggie soup dated 10/19/11 stored in the cooler to be at 52 degrees F on the surface.  When stirred, the temperature in the center was about 58 degrees F.  The soup was discarded and proper cooling and reheating procedures were reviewed.  *Violation Corrected*
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 140°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
*Observed a serving spoon to have duct tape on the handle
*Observed tape on the bottom of the ice scoop
*Observed a few spatulas to be cracked or chipped.
750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.
